question: Checking 30 items one at a time at 40 ms each, stopping at the target: how many ms longer is 'absent' than an average 'present'?
move: Proving something is absent takes far longer than finding it.
trap: No difference, as if each answer required checking every item.
hint: Ask how far through the display the target turns up on average.
steps: 'Present' finds the target halfway on average: 15 × 40 = 600 ms.
reference: Treisman & Gelade, A feature-integration theory of attention, Cognitive Psychology, 1980
